options.execution: Bait as a lure or trick is a genuine sense of the word, but not the one line 14 fixes. 'I had a good bait' in the town, while the master was busy, is about Beauty being fed and rested.

options.value: He is rushing home to get his dinner.
options.execution: Dinner is nowhere in the passage, and he is going away from his house rather than towards it.

options.value: He is sorry at once for knocking the rabbit over.
options.execution: Line 26 has him 'gone before they could think of a reply', which leaves no room for the remorse this asserts.

explanationPatch.hintCore: Read line 23 again. Which word shows how he feels about being held up?
explanationPatch.walkScript: Line 23 gives two words: 'impatient and contemptuous'. Impatient means he does not want to wait. Lines 19 and 20 show why: he is full of the joy of spring. So he will not stop for anyone. He bowls the rabbit over and is gone in one rush.
